content.label: This is a great app but given the crappy battery life of iPhones, it would be nice to not have to rely on my iPhone all day to use this app. A web version would be very convenient!
Beautifully designed. Simple. Innovative features. So many nice touches.
Très bonne app mais il manque la possibilité de mettre des pièces jointes aux tâches.

Just started using it and it’s a definitely improvement on the Things 2, which I abandoned due to slow updates. Great UI and solid Siri implantation. 

Odd bug: keep getting a flash of black as I move between screens.

I would love to see a dark mode implemented somehow. And also the option to add pictures as well. 

Looking forward to the updates in the future.

Liked Things 2, as a good todo list, better than others I tried.  But Things 3 is a game changer.  Love the email to Things, instant syncing, and auto backup.

Think the pricing is high - separate for each device, and high for iPad/Iphone combo.  But, with family sharing permitted, a reasonable value.  I do not keep my to do list on my computer, as it doesn’t go everywhere with me!  The iPad sits next to my laptop computer when I am working anyways, particularly if I am working without an additional monitor.

title.label: Good design, but lacking in features

content.label: I think this app is really overrated. Back in the days, it used to be the gold standard for to-do apps on iOS, but today it has a nice looking design and nothing more. It lacks many features that other free apps have, such as geo-fenced alerts.

title.label: One of the best digital organizers I’ve used

content.label:
I have been a things person for nearly as long as the app has existed. I moved to paper journaling a year and a half ago and that reinforced some good review habits and planning. I’m torn about whether I will return to digital planning, but if I do, this is the app with out a doubt. 

(But pretty please a web app portal, I am a windows user)

I rarely write reviews or rate apps but I found myself recommending it to everyone who is asking about to-do apps. I never would have thought I would be okay with paying $30 for an app but this is well worth it. Gone are the days when I was installing and deleting to-do apps.
Unreal app. So clean. Attention to detail is incredible. I bought all 3 versions.

Things 3 has so many useful, handy features it’s hard to describe them all. This is a well organized app that keeps you focused but is simple enough that you concentrate on getting your work done rather than fidgeting with your todo list. Drag and drop capabilities are great. First thing in the morning I review my list and order it in the way I want to tackle items. And I can change their order easily throughout the day. And the This Evening option is great for those things you want to leave for later. 
All in all a well thought out app. Well worth paying for the premium versions. I have it on my iPhones, iPad and MacBook.
Literally one of the best apps I’ve used. Makes managing life much much easier. And does it in a beautiful way.

title.label: Apple screwed up Reminders on Apple Watch

content.label:
You install Reminders on your AWatch and a complication on watch face. Then you expect Reminders to react like it does on your iPhone. Wrong! Completely the opposite actually. On iPhone at due time the reminder notification shows and stays there until you complete the task. On AWatch the notification shows a few hours before due time and disappears at due time. Then you don’t see that you have a task not completed unless you specifically go in the app. I contacted Apple and they say that’s not a bug. I agree: it’s not a bug, it’s a total screwup of design and implementation that makes the app totally useless on AWatch. 

Things 3 works and performs as expected on AWatch.

title.label: Love the app but why no iCloud??

content.label: I love the new things app. However, please bring back the option to backup to iCloud instead of your own servers.

Easy, useful, intuitive and smart.  
I learn about it in an article and went for it.  A little pricy , and should be shared witting our IPad and iPhone instead of 2 purchases.  This is why it worth 4 stars.
Combined with David Allen book, GTD, i will lower the stress and get things done!

I purchased this app believing it was too good to be true on all the reviews and I have only an iPhone right now and it works very well .

Great Job Guys  :)
I feel like I got a little ripped off that a $13.99 app isn’t actually a universal app so I have to pay for it, which is an additional $27.99 in Canada!  The app is nice but this leaves a sour taste.

The app has lots of promise, a nice layout, and the features I like. But the functionality of it is limited in that I cannot sync to a windows machine. For that reason I won’t use it as much as I would like.

title.label: If you are hesitant to pick a task manager, get this

content.label: I have used different to-do app, omnifocus wunderlist and todolist. I used things 2 as well, but with this brand-new things 3,By far,is the simplest and cleanest to-do app out there!
Loved Things, love Things 3 even more!

I have been searching for a way to combine my “getting things done” productivity world, and my “outliner world” where I plan projects. Things is the closest app I have found to bring these two worlds together in a way that is functional, beautiful and intuitive. 

I love the tagging, dates, inbox, and headings. The reason I wrote “Almost” perfect is that I want to be able to collapse headings, areas, and notes (under project titles). Without the ability to collapse these the work environment can get cluttered.
App is intuitive and useful. Nice that it synchs up between iPhone and iPad... iPad version a bit pricy (30$) but seems worthwhile...

- Love the new UI ❤️
- Using Things3 is delightful every step of the way.
- Realllllllly appreciate the drag and drop in iPad!  It is infinitely useful turning emails into Todos.
- Would really like someway for that same feature to be added in iPhone.  If I can turn emails into Todos, without having to wait until I have my iPad hand then it would be even better

Web APIs would be a nice “next step”.
- Integrations with Zapier, email, other collaboration/ messaging apps would be a great addition.

Playing with app on and off for a few days and I think I can centralize so many things! This could be a life changer! The cost seems rather high and unreasonable to not share across platforms, so loses a star.
The new Things on iOS 11 with Siri integration rocks. It’s the app I’ve been waiting for for ages.

title.label: Best productivity app I've ever used

content.label: I am a planner person, I work off lists (analog and digital) all the time and if I don't have my lists, you best believe I'm getting nothing done and feel like a lost puppy. Enter this app: Things, I just purchased it today, entered everything I needed to do (I have my wedding in 5 days!!) and I feel like I can rule the world. I WISH I looked and found this app years ago. It's very streamlined and has absolutely everything I need in terms of list-making, creating projects with notes and their own to-do lists, creating days where a task sits or deadline, repeating tasks, having tags and syncing calendars to the app. It has everything I've ever needed in a productivity app and more that I didn't know would be useful!! I LOVE THIS APP!! Low key hoping it can help me get the rest of my life together :-)
I would have thought that a TASK app would allow you to have reoccurring TASKS, but nope. Kicking myself for buying this.

Overall not too bad, although it provides similar functionality with Apple's Reminders. I am surprised that simple list features like duplicates identification and removal, and alphabetical sorting are missing. That's why I don't find it useful for shopping lists, for example.

And yeah, it's overpriced for what it does. The prices for IPad and Mac are astronomical!

10/10 integration with calendars etc.
My new go to for organizing everything.

I have used earlier versions of Things in my search for the perfect to-do app. Evernote is incredibly flexible, but too complicated for my needs. LifeTopix has a beautiful interface, but I got distracted with where and how file info. Clear is incredibly simple.

Things 3 has evolved into the perfect balance simplicity and flexibility. I don't always have time to dig deep into an app to enter a to-do in the right place, but the inbox takes care of that.

- Helps keep me on track 
- multiple project list
- Great logging system
- does what it says
- sync between multiple devices
- Beautiful design and interface

Couldn't live without it....well I could, but I'd be less organized!
I follow the GTD workflow, and Things 3 is the perfect complement. Not only is it super functional, it looks beautiful and is actually fun to use. Look no further, this is the app for you.

This app has has problems with every update. It shows up in the list of apps to be updated but when I choose to allow it to update it comes back a few minutes later with an error message that it can't update. There are typically quite a few other apps to be updated and the other apps update successfully but Things3 comes back with the error message. Eventually, after several days it does update. Let's see if it does better with the next update.

title.label: This app is simple, beautiful, and powerful!

content.label: This is s must have app!

I love the experience of using the app - probably the most delightful to-do list app I've used. Very functional as well, with some advanced features. And the widget is very useful!

I've deducted one star for a few features I miss:
- full integration with Siri, which is supposed to be coming with iOS 11. 
 - inability to set reminders/due dates when creating todos from the Share Sheet (using Add to Things icon).
- there's a bug where if I tap out of an empty todo, it doesn't delete itself. Why would I ever need an empty todo?

Overall, it's an amazing app. A bit further to go in features, which I'm sure is a matter of time. Thank you!
This app got me into the realms of GTD. love the design and fluidity. Couple small nitpicks - no x-URL clickable links, no ability to save attachments, no geobased tags.
Third version is just perfect for all my to-do needs 👍

I own Things 3 on macOS, iPhone and iPad and really like it all-round.

My only real gripe is that the Apple Watch app keeps losing sync and stops updating. So the watch complication and app show days-old items that were already marked complete and does not show new items. I have tried uninstalling the app but the problem keeps returning each time. I've emailed support but have not received a reply yet.

UPDATE: I did a little digging and found how to reset the watch sync, but you shouldn't have to do that. And now I feel like I can't trust the watch app because it may fall out of sync at any time unexpectedly and I won't know until I check the iPhone app.
easily the best to-do app i've used. i'm borderline incredulous at how well they did this.

title.label: Perfect blend of Calendar and to do list

content.label: A pricey purchase but it replaced two stock apps and it works so smoothly. Nice clean layout. Easy to learn and use but can also hold tremendous detail. I check it every morning and night and helps keep me on track with everything from big projects to daily appointments. I love it.
Finally found a to do app after so many years, but I don't like the fact you have to pay iPad version again, feel like a rip off

Became the most used app on my phone immediately.  Huge productivity boost since downloading Things 3.  Very simple and easy to use, and the level of detail it allows you to structure into each to-do makes Reminders seem silly in comparison.  Projects function to group related to-do's is brilliant.  Worth the money no hesitation.

title.label: Great design, simple, powerful, and fun.

content.label:
It's strangely difficult to get a todo list app that combines simplicity with a full set of features, and has a friendly feel to it. Things managed to get all three!

The only downside is that there's no sharing of lists, but for personal task management, it's the perfect app. 💅

I use this applications to manage the care I need to give to my patient it is very efficient and I improve the quality of care that I provide. Every patient become a project with task to realize in order to optimize their reestablishment. 

Thanks guys... Keep coding, you are genius!!
Significant features update with calendar integration, flexibility and multi layers within projects and to dos. Love the minimalism and simplicity.
Splendid design and intelligent organizational methods allowable to its users. Recommended to all iPhone, iMac and MacBook Pro, with its use on iPad too. Brilliant!

title.label: In a category of its own

content.label: Tried many productivity, lists, to-do, and all related apps always finding that just something is missing. Not with Things 3; everything you need it does, perfect user interface and workflow. Everything is intuitive. Expensive, but worth every dime.

Previous Things 2 user and many many other task manager apps as well. This app is as close to perfect as I can imagine. I would like to be able to call a number entered in the note by tapping and I miss not being able to link a task to a contact. But just buy it. The other reviewers are not wrong.

title.label: The Best To Do list app

content.label: I HAVE GOTTEN SO MUCH DONE! THANKS!

5 stars does not do this app justice.  It is in another class far superior to Apple's own Reminders and every other organization/to do list app I have experienced.  "Scary" because of the very fast dependency created by an app, this one, that so brilliantly ends the awkwardness of using Reminders, lists in Notes, and Calendar to organize your life!  Incredibly intuitive, this app so easily combines all the simple organizational tasks including Calendar, in one place, all visual, flexible, and with all the well thought out necessary personal options.  The price?  Your personal time saved is worth it.  You need to try it.  You will not go back!
